 Download the app Harden passes Kobe with 51-point display vs. Pacers
 Jonathan Soveta • · Nick Cammett / Getty Images Sport / Getty James Harden scored a season-high 51 points on 15-of-26 shooting as the Cleveland Cavaliers topped the Indiana Pacers in their NBA Cup matchup Friday, 128-119.
 Harden shot 7-of-11 from distance in the win and was a perfect 14-of-14 from the line.
 It's the 11-time All-Star's 26th career game with 50 or more points, breaking a tie with Los Angeles Lakers icon Kobe Bryant for the third-most in NBA history.

 The 37-year-old, whose previous season high was a 32-point performance against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Nov. 11, added six rebounds and six assists in 40 minutes against the Pacers. 
 Harden's 27 second-half points were the most he's recorded in a half since joining the Cavaliers via trade last season from the Los Angeles Clippers.

 The 18th-year vet entered Friday averaging 16.2 points, 6.3 assists, and 4.7 rebounds while shooting a career-low 38.5% from the field.
 With the victory, Cleveland moves to 9-8 on the season and 2-1 in NBA Cup group play, a half-game back of the Miami Heat in the Group B standings.
